newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican gov't nixes Zapatista trip to Mexico City.
newsitem.headline: Mexican gov't nixes Zapatista trip to Mexico City.

text.p: The Mexican government said on Thursday it would not allow a planned trip to Mexico city next month by Zapatista rebel commanders who want to attend an indigenous congress.

Organisers of the event, to be held Oct. 8-12 in the capital, had asked for guarantees of safe conduct for the guerrilla leaders, whose Zapatista National Liberation Army (EZLN) rose up in arms in the southeastern state of Chiapas on New Year's Day 1994.
Representatives of 50 indigenous communities are scheduled to attend the event.
The Zapatistas are mostly Maya Indians from Chiapas, although their best-known figure, Subcommander Marcos, is from a white urban background.

The charismatic, ski-masked Marcos was not expected to try and attend the event although he has expressed interest in travelling to Mexico City and says the law governing peace talks with the government allows the rebels freedom of movement as long as they do not promote armed rebellion.

"They know the law does not permit it," said Marco Antonio Bernal, the head of the government negotiating team at the talks. "There is no chance... The Zapatistas are a group which has arms, which has clandestine activity and definitely do not enjoy the qualities and conditions of just any citizen."
The law governing the talks, passed in March last year, suspends arrest warrants against Marcos and other rebel leaders as long as peace talks continue.
Under its protection Marcos and other leaders have travelled from their jungle bases to the city of San Cristobal de las Casas in Chiapas to take part in the talks.
The government says it does not apply nationwide, however.
The Zapatistas earlier this month suspended the talks and demanded a new government negotiating team, accusing the existing one of "racism", but negotiations are not formally broken off.
The Zapatistas say they wish to become an unarmed, nationwide grass-roots political movement to be called the Zapatista National Liberation Front.
